title: Chow groups and cycle groups commute with a filtered limit of affine base changes in the c = 0 situation
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-setup-base-change with c = 0 and S' = colim_{i in I} S_i a filtered limit of schemes affine over S satisfying the three listed situation conditions, the lemma states that for a quasi-compact X of finite type over S with base changes X' and X_i one has Z_k(X') = colim Z_k(X_i) and CH_k(X') = colim CH_k(X_i) (statement lines 15482-15498). The proof first reduces to the Noetherian case by replacing S by a quasi-compact open over which X -> S factors, so that all schemes in the proof become Noetherian (proof lines 15500-15506). Surjectivity of colim Z_k(X_i) -> Z_k(X') is proved by descending an integral closed subscheme Z' of delta'-dimension k along Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-finite-presentation and Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, replacing Z_i by the scheme theoretic image of Z' -> X_i, and matching dimensions with Lemma labelled lemma-dimension-base-change (proof lines 15508-15528). Injectivity is proved by testing a cycle alpha_i whose base change to X' vanishes: since each base change Z'_j -> Z_j is flat and dominant, the coefficient of a dominating component is nonzero, so every Z'_j must be empty, and then Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-limit-nonempty kills alpha_i at some transition map (proof lines 15530-15549). The Chow group statement follows by the same strategy: surjectivity from the cycle level result, and injectivity by descending the integral subschemes W'_l and the rational functions f'_l that exhibit alpha' as a sum of divisors, using Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-opens and Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-section, with the comparison of the divisor coefficients n_{l,j} = n_{i,l,j} reduced to the order comparison along the flat local ring map O_{W_{i,l},xi} -> O_{W'_l,xi'} and Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-pullback-module (proof lines 15551-15618); one step in that comparison is dismissed as 'for some i' >= i by an easy argument we omit' (proof line 15592), while the rest of the argument is written out. Descending cycles, divisors and rational functions through a filtered limit and matching the orders along a flat local ring map is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
